brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Getting Started with ESource Bookkeeping Tool

questions.question: What three things make this bookkeeping tool different from other tools?
choices: It carries your brand, your data stays with you, and everything is locked to your firm
It is free, it works offline, and it automatically files taxes
It requires no internet, it syncs to the cloud, and it handles payroll
It integrates with all banks, it stores data on ESource servers, and it is open to all users
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—your firm's brand appears on reports, bank data never leaves your computers, and encryption ensures only approved staff can access the books.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The tool does require internet at least weekly, does not store data on ESource servers, and is locked to your firm's approved staff only. Review Slide 2 for the three core differences.

questions.question: How long does a 6-digit sign-in code remain valid?
choices: It never expires
10 minutes
24 hours
30 days
questions.feedback_correct: That's correct—the code works for ten minutes, so you need to enter it promptly after receiving it in your email.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The code is time-limited to keep your account secure. Review Slide 3 to see exactly how long you have to use it.

questions.question: What happens to a staff member's computer when they are removed from the License tab?
choices: They can still access the books if they know the password
The books lock at the next check-in, even if it is their personal laptop
They have 30 days to transfer the books to a new computer
Nothing changes until they try to sign in again
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—removing someone from the License tab immediately protects your client list by locking the books on their computer at the next check-in.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The tool automatically locks books on a removed staff member's computer for security, rather than relying on passwords or delayed actions. This is why owners should remove departing staff the same day they leave. See Slide 4.

questions.question: What must happen before you can add a new client to your firm's account?
choices: Your internet connection must be active so the tool can verify your plan limit
You must wait for your owner to approve the new client
The client must first upload their bank statements
You must have filled in all of your own Setup information
questions.feedback_correct: Right—adding a client requires internet because the tool checks your firm's plan limit across all staff at that moment.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Internet is needed at the moment of adding a client so the tool can verify your plan is not over the limit. Review Slide 5 for how adding a client works.

questions.question: Which file format works best when uploading bank statements from non-Wells Fargo banks?
choices: CSV only, because it is the smallest file size
Quicken or QuickBooks files work best because they include the account number and balance
PDF files, because they match Wells Fargo's format
OFX only, because it is the newest standard
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—Quicken (QFX) and QuickBooks (QBO) files are best because they include account numbers and ending balances, which the tool needs to verify.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While CSV, QFX, QBO, and OFX formats all work, Quicken and QuickBooks formats include the account number and ending balance, making them the best choice. See Slide 6 for details.

questions.question: What does leaving "Remember" checked after answering an Ask Client question accomplish?
choices: It sends a reminder email to the client
It creates a rule so similar lines sort themselves automatically next month
It saves your answer to the cloud for backup
It locks the transaction so no one else can change it
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—checking "Remember" creates a rule that automatically sorts similar lines in future months, reducing the number of questions you need to ask.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The "Remember" feature is about building automation through rules, not backup or permissions. By checking it when you categorize a line, the tool learns and sorts similar transactions in the future. Review Slide 7.

questions.question: You set up a client reminder for day 3 of each month, and the client adds the calendar file to their phone. What happens next?
choices: The client receives text messages from your firm every month on day 3
Their phone reminds them every month to send last month's statements, and you only set this up once
The client must re-download the file each month or the reminders stop
The reminder comes from ESource software, not from your firm
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—once the client adds the calendar file to their phone, it reminds them every month, and this is a one-time setup on your end.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The calendar reminder is a recurring, automatic reminder on the client's own device after the one-time setup. It is not a text message, does not require monthly re-downloads, and comes from your firm. See Slide 9.

questions.question: Your firm's owner has not turned on automatic email reminders. Where does your data go when you click "Email client" on the Status tab?
choices: It is sent to ESource servers and forwarded to the client
Your own email app opens with the message already typed, so it comes from your firm's address
It is stored in the tool's secure queue until the owner enables automatic email
It is encrypted and held in the backup file until manual sending is approved
questions.feedback_correct: That's right—clicking "Email client" opens your own email app with the message pre-written, so the client knows it comes directly from your firm, not from the software.
questions.feedback_incorrect: When you use the "Email client" or "Text client" buttons, your own Messages or email app opens with the message ready to send from your account. This is different from the automatic email feature. Review Slide 10.

questions.question: What is the relationship between your firm's plan tier and the number of Help assistant minutes available each month?
choices: Every plan includes unlimited Help assistant minutes
Your firm gets ten help minutes per client book every month, and the owner can see this on the License tab
Help minutes are purchased separately and do not affect your plan tier
Each staff member gets five minutes per month regardless of plan
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—your firm receives ten Help assistant minutes per client book each month, and the owner can track used and remaining minutes on the License tab.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Help assistant minutes are included with your plan and tracked per client book. The owner can see this information on the License tab to manage usage across the firm. Review Slide 4.

questions.question: A backup file from your firm is accidentally left on a lost laptop. Why does this not put your client data at risk?
choices: Backup files are uploaded to ESource servers automatically, so the laptop file is just a local copy
ESource support can track the laptop's location and retrieve the file
Backup files are locked (encrypted) to your firm, so a lost file cannot be read by anyone else
The file is only readable if the person has your firm's plan password
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—backup files are encrypted and locked to your firm, so even if a backup file is lost, it remains unreadable to anyone outside your firm.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The security of backup files comes from encryption that is specific to your firm, not from server upload or password protection. This is why following the 3-2-1 backup rule keeps your data safe. See Slide 14.
